paragraphs: Azuga sells GPS fleet tracking and dual-facing dashcam software meant to keep vehicles, assets and drivers safe. The company argues that such software should improve safety and not only day-to-day operations. It pitches the product as simple to use, affordable, customizable, and easy to install.

The company frames the work as a four-part improvement process folded into daily fleet operations. Driver scoring is meant to show managers and drivers alike how safely they are driving. A mobile app included in the subscription gives administrators and drivers separate views. For tools and small equipment, Bluetooth beacons are picked up by the company's cellular asset trackers. One tracker can detect and report on fifty beacons at a time. Vehicles that leave the factory with built-in telematics can connect to the platform without aftermarket hardware.

Azuga says customers have relied on it since 2013 for GPS fleet tracking and asset tracking. Insurance companies use its telematics data to measure and price risk in commercial vehicle portfolios. The company also says it works with government agencies on how transportation taxes, emissions data and tolls are collected. States and municipalities, it states, use the data to understand traffic patterns and road surface conditions.

quote.text: Azuga also helps states and municipalities understand traffic patterns and road surface conditions to improve infrastructure planning and upkeep.
